In this notebook I generate the plots that show $RMSE$ differences between our cluster-then-predict method and the other model variants. In essence, this data is already pre-computed so this notebook does not offer any new insights about how to use the library. However, these plots are included in the paper so I am being transparent about how they were generated. 

In the future I will also add a demo notebook showing how the `data.json` and `results_universal_vs_cluster.json` data was generated.

#### CTP against the single XGBoost
```{python}
PATH_TO_DATA = "/Users/legariapena.j/Documents/imageable-2026/imageable/data/universal_vs_cluster/results_universal_vs_cluster.json"

import json
with open(PATH_TO_DATA) as f:
    data = json.load(f)

#Collect the RMSE values obtained with the CTP and with the single-XGBoost models.

cluster_then_predict_rmses = [x["cluster_then_predict_rmse"] for x in data]
single_xgboost_rmses = [x["universal_model_rmse"] for x in data]

#Differences in RMSE across seeds
deltas = [y-x for x,y in zip(cluster_then_predict_rmses, single_xgboost_rmses, strict = False)]


from imageable.visualization.data_visualization import plot_styled_histogram

DRACULA_PALETTE = {
    "comment": "#6272a4",
    "purple": "#bd93f9",
    "red": "#ff5555",
    "green": "#50fa7b",
    "yellow": "#f1fa8c",
    "pink": "#ff79c6",
    "cyan": "#8be9fd",
    "blue": "#44475a"
}

plot = plot_styled_histogram(
    deltas,
    title = "RMSE Diference (Single XGBoost - Cluster Then Predict)",
    bins = 10, 
    color = DRACULA_PALETTE["purple"],
    better_left_label ="universal model",
    better_right_label = "cluster-then-predict", 
    xlim = (-0.75, 0.75), 
    right_annotation_color = DRACULA_PALETTE["blue"],
    left_annotation_color = DRACULA_PALETTE["blue"],
    ylim = (0,13), 
    savepath = "/Users/legariapena.j/Documents/imageable-2026/imageable/data/universal_vs_cluster/cluster_vs_universal_histogram.png"
)
```
Let's show the p-values for a wilcoxon signed rank and binomial tests.

```{python}
from scipy.stats import binomtest, wilcoxon
import numpy as np

def get_wilcoxon_and_sign_tests(deltas_data):
    deltas_data = np.asarray(deltas_data)

    w = wilcoxon(deltas_data, alternative = "greater", zero_method = "wilcox")

    wins = int((deltas_data > 0).sum())
    n = int((deltas_data !=0).sum())
    s = binomtest(wins, n = n, p = 0.5, alternative = "greater")


    return w.pvalue, s.pvalue

w_p_value, binomial_p_value = get_wilcoxon_and_sign_tests(deltas)

print(f"Wilcoxon p = {w_p_value}")
print(f"Binomial p = {binomial_p_value}")

```


#### CTP against the footprint-based model

```{python}

footprint_model_rmses = [x["footprint_model_rmse"] for x in data]
footprint_deltas = [y-x for x,y in zip(cluster_then_predict_rmses, footprint_model_rmses, strict = False)]

plot = plot_styled_histogram(
    footprint_deltas,
    title = "RMSE Difference (Footprint Model - Cluster Then Predict)", 
    bins = 20, 
    color = "#8be9fd", 
    edgecolor = DRACULA_PALETTE["comment"], 
    better_left_label = "footprint_model", 
    better_right_label = "cluster-then-predict",

    ylim = (0,10),

)
```
